correctness.rationale: For fixed n>=3 and Pareto type I at unit scale, checking the two largest smaller lengths for each possible largest stick reduces triangle-freedom exactly to nonnegative slacks (up to null ties). The inverse recursion has unit Jacobian and x_i=F_i+sum_{j<=i}b_ij u_j, with b_ii=1 and nonnegative coefficients. Changing to alpha u cancels alpha^n in the ordered density. The scaled integrand converges to exp(-sum c_j v_j) and is dominated for alpha>=2 by the integrable product of (1+v_i/(2F_i))^(-2), since (1+t/alpha)^alpha grows with alpha. Its limiting mass and Scheffé prove the probability equivalent and the full product-exponential TV law; the rates are strictly decreasing by comparing successive nonnegative Fibonacci columns and their extra diagonal term. The resulting unscaled lengths concentrate on the Fibonacci vector. At the other endpoint log lengths are exponential, and the ordered log spacings are independent with rates (n-i)alpha. Integrating the event z<h(y) against their density gives r_i r_(i+1) times pi²/12 with O_n(alpha³) error, since yh and h² are integrable. Overlaps are O_n(alpha³) at adjacent indices by bounding the third gap by log 2, and O_n(alpha⁴) otherwise by independence. Inclusion–exclusion and the sum of (n-i)(n-i-1) give the stated coefficient. Given a triangle, multiple adjacent violations have probability O_n(alpha); conditioning on a unique index instead of its single event changes its gap law by O_n(alpha) in TV. The single-event normalized density converges by Scheffé to the stated uniform density on the curved gap domain, independent of the limiting index. No growing-n uniformity is needed. The independent finite replay `python3 /workspace/reviews/check_1.py` gave the exact n=3,4 constants 4/3 and 108/65, verified the 3/4,1/4 mark weights for n=4, and quadrature gave 0.822467033424113 for the gap domain area. These are finite checks, not proofs of TV. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The endpoint probability alone does not locate the rare configurations. At large shape the theorem identifies the constrained Fibonacci minimizer and exact joint fluctuations around it; at small shape it separates the likely violation index from the observable geometry of the two short log gaps. These are useful local descriptions of two different rare events and do not duplicate the moving-shape Poisson location law.
